tonight.headline: Nothing has kicked off. The deadline that matters is 01:00 tonight.
body: Week 2 has not started. ESPN has Panda Attack 125.4 to your 118.5 and gives you a 47% chance. They reset their lineup at 15:25 UTC today, after this morning's brief — Dak Prescott now starts over Jalen Hurts — so their number is up on what you saw earlier.

Your clock is the waiver run at 01:00 tonight, Mexico City. The JuiceJam offer has to be sent before it, because the Coker claim drops Matthew Stafford, who is half of that offer. After that the only move left is McLaurin into the flex before Sunday 14:05.

case.label: What their change does
case.body: Prescott was held to 175 yards on 34 attempts by the Giants in Week 1 and now plays at home against Washington; Hurts had a three-touchdown opener and draws Tennessee as a heavy favourite. Swapping one for the other is roughly neutral on paper — the projection moved by 1.4, not by a lineup's worth.

case.label: The swing you control none of
case.body: Josh Allen plays Thursday night and locks before anyone else. Detroit just allowed 410 passing yards to Tyler Shough and are missing both starting safeties. A big Thursday closes most of the roughly 7-point gap by itself.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: McLaurin into the flex is worth about 3.1 projected points and is the only lineup lever you have. If the JuiceJam trade lands before Sunday, McLaurin is gone and Tuten stays in — the gap then stays close to where ESPN has it.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Send before 01:00 tonight, Mexico City — the Coker claim removes Stafford from this offer
doFirst.title: Send the JuiceJam offer now: McLaurin + Stafford for DeVonta Smith
doFirst.subtitle: Recomputed on this afternoon's file: +21.8 for you, +3.8 for them. It dies at 01:00 if it is still unanswered.

case.label: Why the clock is tonight
case.body: The Coker claim below drops Stafford when waivers process at 07:00 UTC. If JuiceJam have not accepted by then, the offer is void because you no longer own half of it. Send it now so they have the whole afternoon; if it is accepted first, the two-for-one opens a roster seat and the Coker claim needs no drop at all.

case.label: Why they say yes
case.body: Their quarterback is Jared Goff, 26 of 39 for 206 yards and two scores in an overtime win over New Orleans — solid, and at 277.8 the lowest season projection of any starting quarterback in Chem (earlier runs called it second-lowest; the file says lowest). Stafford is the reigning MVP at 303.4 despite a scoreless opener against a 49ers defense that shut him down. They give up a starting receiver, and DJ Moore sits on their bench at 209.0 to cover it.

case.label: What you are selling, checked today
case.body: McLaurin drew 4 targets in Week 1 to Stefon Diggs's 9, and third-round rookie Antonio Williams matched his 4. RotoWire still calls McLaurin the expected No. 1; the target split says the room is shared. Stafford cannot start for you in a one-quarterback league behind Allen.

case.label: What you are buying, corrected
case.body: This morning's case called Smith a volume buy. That overstated it: Smith caught 3 of 6 for 53, and Hurts spread 14 completions across six players with nobody above four catches (RotoWire). Smith is Philadelphia's top receiver after the A.J. Brown trade, but in a spread-it-around offense. The deal is consolidation into the best player, not a bet on a target hog.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: Both sides recompute to exactly this morning's numbers — 2070.3 to 2092.1 for you, 1966.4 to 1970.2 for them — for the third run running. seasonProj is not moving, so this is priced on August's opinion. On this week's projections they lose 0.3, which is the likeliest reason it gets declined. It has been live since Sunday with no trade activity in the log.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: They decline or let it lapse past 07:00 UTC; or Diggs's target share collapses by Week 3 while McLaurin's recovers, which would make this a sale at the bottom.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Waivers clear 01:00 Wednesday, Mexico City · order this claim first
doFirst.title: Claim Jalen Coker, drop Matthew Stafford
doFirst.subtitle: The ankle boot is precautionary by his own account and he says he practises Wednesday. Chem priority resets, so a miss costs nothing.

case.label: The player
case.body: 8 catches on 9 targets for 138 yards and two touchdowns in Week 1, a career game played mostly after he rolled the ankle in the first quarter. It was his second straight game over 130 yards, counting last January's wild-card loss. Bryce Young is throwing to him.

case.label: The ankle
case.body: Photographed in a walking boot on Monday. Coker called it precautionary, said he does not expect to miss time and plans to practise Wednesday; NBC, Yahoo, DraftKings Network and Heavy all carry the same account. Nothing new has been reported since. Carolina's first practice report arrives after this claim processes, so you are claiming blind — on purpose, because a failed Chem claim costs nothing lasting.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Stafford, who is 92.6% rostered, and this disagrees with the market on purpose: Chem starts one quarterback, Allen is the QB1 in this scoring, and the wire holds several starting quarterbacks for Allen's Week 7 bye, Trevor Lawrence among them. Stafford is only worth keeping as a trade chip — which is why the JuiceJam offer goes out first.

case.label: The matchup risk
case.body: Atlanta's defense was top 10 in pressure rate in Week 1 by NBC's read, and Carolina are already missing two starting offensive linemen. That argues for a quieter Sunday than the opener, not against the claim.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Coker is limited or does not practise in Wednesday's report, or carries a designation into Sunday; or Tetairoa McMillan reasserts as the clear No. 1 and Coker's target share falls under about 18% across Weeks 2-3.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Waivers clear 01:00 Wednesday, Mexico City · order this claim second
doFirst.title: Claim the Ravens defense, drop the Jaguars defense
doFirst.subtitle: Still worth the free claim, but today's board has the gap narrower than this morning's did.

case.label: Why Baltimore
case.body: They host New Orleans, whose quarterback Tyler Shough looked poor in the first half of Week 1 by NBC's read, and whose second passing option is Devaughn Vele. RotoBaller's Week 2 waiver column lists the Ravens first among defenses to add. They are 89.9% rostered nationally and free here.

case.label: Why the gap is smaller than it was
case.body: This morning's case rested on Lindy's having Baltimore 2nd and Jacksonville 9th. NBC's board, published at 15:45 UTC today, puts both in the same tier and says Jacksonville may still sneak into the top 10 at Denver. Jacksonville are also without defensive end BJ Green. The move is still right; it is a smaller upgrade than it looked.

case.label: Order it second
case.body: You are priority 5 of 10 and priority resets weekly. Put Coker first. If Coker is awarded, this one probably fails and Jacksonville stay — an acceptable fallback, not a loss.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Baltimore finish outside the top 12 defenses in Week 2, or Jacksonville finish top 5 at Denver. Either says this was churn on a one-week board.

action.label: Claim Ravens D/ST · drop Jaguars D/ST

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Before Sunday 14:05, Mexico City — Jacksonville kick off first of the two
doFirst.title: Start Terry McLaurin in the flex, bench Bhayshul Tuten
doFirst.subtitle: About three projected points, and today's usage data makes the case stronger than this morning's.

case.label: The flex is RB/WR
case.body: Chem's slot 3 takes a back or a receiver. McLaurin projects 12.5, Tuten 9.4.

case.label: What the backfield numbers show
case.body: Tuten led Jacksonville with 48% of snaps and 15 carries, but Chris Rodriguez Jr. took every red-zone rush and every goal-to-go snap (Fantasy Life) and ran more routes than Tuten did. DraftSharks expects third-down back LeQuint Allen to return to the mix, and calls Denver a less favourable spot. A lead back with no goal line and no passing downs is the weakest asset type in full PPR.

case.label: What McLaurin gets
case.body: Washington go to Dallas, whose defense allowed the most passing yards in the league last season (RotoWire). DraftSharks calls it the more favourable secondary of his next two games. Jayden Daniels is throwing.

case.label: Not in tension with the trade
case.body: The JuiceJam offer sells McLaurin on the season. This is Sunday. If the trade lands first, this card is moot and Tuten stays in.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Washington list McLaurin as limited or questionable this week; or Jacksonville give Tuten the goal-line work at Denver; or the JuiceJam trade is accepted.

whatWentWrong.title: The trade case oversold DeVonta Smith's volume
whatWentWrong.lead: Six targets, three catches, and an offense that spreads the ball around. The deal still works, for a different reason.

case.label: What was written
case.body: This morning's case called Smith the volume-good, results-bad profile the strategy file says to buy.

case.label: What the box score says
case.body: 3 of 6 for 53. Hurts completed 14 passes to six different players and nobody caught more than four; Dallas Goedert and Dontayvion Wicks both out-gained Smith. That is not a target hog having a bad day.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Smith drawing 9 or more targets at Tennessee would restore the original read. Until then the trade stands on consolidation and on Stafford's value to a Goff team — which is why the card above was rewritten, not withdrawn.

whatWentWrong.title: Tuten's problem is routes as well as the goal line
whatWentWrong.lead: Rodriguez had every red-zone rush and every goal-to-go snap — and ran more routes than Tuten.

case.label: The numbers
case.body: Two trackers split slightly: 36% versus 40% route share (Zachariason), 40% versus 48% (Metz). Both have Rodriguez ahead. The morning brief only had the red-zone half.

case.label: Why it matters here
case.body: It is the reason McLaurin takes the flex, and the reason the flex call is firmer this afternoon than it was this morning.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Tuten getting a goal-line carry or out-running Rodriguez on routes at Denver.

whatWentWrong.title: The Baltimore-over-Jacksonville gap shrank on a second board
whatWentWrong.lead: NBC puts both defenses in the same tier. The claim is still free; expect less from it.

case.label: What changed
case.body: The morning claim rested on one ranking, Lindy's. NBC's board, published after it, has Baltimore and Jacksonville side by side in tier 2 of 5.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Jacksonville finishing top 5 at Denver, which would make the claim churn.

trades.theirGainLine: Their gain is +3.8 on the season — they swap Jared Goff's 277.8 for the reigning MVP's 303.4 and keep DJ Moore to cover the receiver slot. Say it in the message.

youGet.name: DeVonta Smith
youGet.detail: WR PHI · 240.1 season · starting at their slot 4

case.label: Their slot column, read today
case.body: Goff at slot 0 is their only quarterback. Smith and CeeDee Lamb start at receiver; DJ Moore (209.0) sits at slot 20 and is the backfill. This asks for a starter, and it works for them only because Moore covers it.

case.label: The shape
case.body: Two-for-one where you receive the best player. The seat you open refills from a wire that still has several startable receivers on it.

case.label: Their quarterback, checked
case.body: Goff went 26 of 39 for 206 and two TDs, winning in overtime. Stafford was shut down by San Francisco in Week 1 but is the reigning MVP and projects 25.6 more season points than Goff in this scoring.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: It clears on the season only; on this week's projections they lose 0.3. seasonProj has not moved across three runs, so both numbers may be August's. And Smith's Week 1 was 6 targets in a spread offense, not the volume this case once claimed.

trades.copyText: Hi — Jared Goff is your only QB and projects 277.8 rest-of-season. I'll send you Matthew Stafford (reigning MVP, 303.4) plus Terry McLaurin for DeVonta Smith. On season projections that's +3.8 for you, and DJ Moore on your bench covers Smith's spot. I get one receiver, you get the QB upgrade and a WR. Need an answer before tonight's waiver run — interested?

worthALook.name: Tyler Loop
worthALook.lead: K4 this week against Boswell's K17. Still a watch, because the hold's own trigger has not fired.

case.label: The gap
case.body: PFN's Week 2 kicker board: Loop 4th hosting New Orleans, Boswell 17th at New England. ESPN's weekly projections differ by 0.9 — under the one-point bar the strategy file sets.

case.label: Why not now
case.body: You already have two claims queued, and the Boswell hold on record says to move only if he finishes outside the top 20 or Pittsburgh's implied total stays low. Neither has happened; this is one week of rankings.

case.label: When to act
case.body: If Boswell finishes outside the top 20 kickers this week, claim Loop next Wednesday when priority has reset and nothing better is competing.

worthALook.name: Stefon Diggs
worthALook.lead: Nine targets in Week 1 to McLaurin's four — the receiver the JuiceJam sale is built on.

case.label: The role
case.body: Diggs ran 65.8% of routes and drew a target on 36% of them (CBS), mostly from the slot. He is 83.8% rostered nationally and free here.

case.label: Why it is not a claim
case.body: You cut him on 12 September for Brian Thomas Jr.; re-adding him three days later is the reversal the log records as churn, and the only open seat this week is spoken for by Coker. The standing hold says a fallback claim reopens only if Thomas is ruled out.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Thomas ruled out for Week 2, or the JuiceJam trade landing and opening a seat — then Diggs is the first free-agent look next week.

doNotChase.name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
doNotChase.lead: He does own Jacksonville's goal line after all — and it is still not enough in this scoring.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Six carries for 23 yards and no target in a game Jacksonville led 31-0. The goal-line work is real — every red-zone rush and goal-to-go snap — but that was one carry.

case.label: Why it is wrong for this roster
case.body: Full PPR pays receptions first. A short-yardage back with no catches collects the least valuable touches there are, and you already own Tuten in the same backfield.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Tuten missing time, or Rodriguez turning goal-line work into two or more touchdowns a week for a month.

doNotChase.name: Eddy Pineiro
doNotChase.lead: 84.8% rostered and free, and the kicker you cut for Boswell a week ago.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: K12 on PFN's Week 2 board against Boswell's K17 — a handful of places, well under a point. Loop at K4 is the only kicker worth a move.

case.label: The pattern
case.body: The log already carries this slot reversing twice across both leagues as churn. Re-adding the man you dropped on 8 September is the same move a third time.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing about Pineiro. If the slot moves, it moves to Loop.
